why: 2 Nephi 12-24 reads as a highlight reel of lone Isaiah verses; consolidate to the famous few under one bridge, clearing the per-chapter bridges (the dropped 17:13 and 23:19 bridges would otherwise migrate onto 19:6 and 25:1)

bridges.2 Nephi 12:2: Nephi copies thirteen chapters of Isaiah (Isaiah 2–14): judgments on proud Judah, Isaiah's call in the temple, a promised royal child, and Babylon's fall. Only a few of the best-known lines are kept.

why: 1 Ne 8:7 'as I followed him' follows nothing; restore the man in white bidding Lehi follow
1 Ne 10:2 ends 'concerning the Jews—' and 10:4 does not complete it
Lehi's covenant refrain (keep commandments, prosper in the land) missing from his final exhortation
2 Ne 4:15 'upon these I write' points at nothing; 4:14 contrasts the other plates
Restore a strong line of Nephi's psalm (robe of thy righteousness)
2 Ne 6:8 'concerning these words' refers to Isaiah verses the reader never saw

bridges.2 Nephi 6:8: Jacob reads Isaiah's promise that the Gentiles will carry Israel's scattered children home, with kings and queens as their nursing parents.

why: 2 Ne 9:1 ends with a dash that 9:3 does not complete
Restore 9:22, which completes 9:21's thought on why he suffers
Restore the strong atonement verse 9:26 between 9:25 and the 'But wo' of 9:27
2 Ne 11:7 'For if there be no Christ' does not follow from 11:2
Restore the well-known 32:5 (the Holy Ghost will show you all things)
Jacob 1:10 ends mid-sentence with a dash; 1:11 completes it and explains 'the second king' in 1:15
